Binti Rising Initiative  ·  A Photographic Monograph
Nairobi · MMXXVI

From Silence,
She Rises.

In Kibera, Mathare and Kawangware, the Binti Rising Initiative runs a peer-led mentorship programme — the Journey to Wholeness — for adolescent girls and young women aged 15 to 25. This monograph follows one arc through fourteen photographs from the Nairobi team's own camera roll: circle, classroom, voice, craft, proof, rise.

Peer-ledJourney to Wholeness (JTW)Ages 15–25 Kibera — Mathare — KawangwareDPA 2019 compliant
I.The Circle

Nothing begins with a lesson.

It begins with a circle — hands joined, names said aloud, the day's fears set in the middle where everyone can see them. Peer mentors lead; adults hold the space. Attendance across the three communities runs at ninety per cent and above, but the truer metric is simpler: they come back.

II.The Classroom

The work moves through classrooms and halls.

One week it is letters and stories on a chalkboard; the next, a conversation about the body, consent and health that the syllabus never scheduled. Sessions are built for 15-to-25-year-olds — old enough to be trusted with the truth.

III.The Voice
“Girls are to be married off.”
Read aloud — then struck through, together. Session flipchart, Plate 08.

On a paper flipchart, myths die in public. Facilitators write down what the street says; the circle answers back, line by line — ten steps to help a friend, myths crossed out in marker. When a girl takes the charts and stands, the session changes owners. That is precisely the point of a peer-led model.

IV.The Craft & The Team

Between circles, hands stay busy.

Crayon on paper. A film afternoon. Handball drills. Comics that teach in the street's own language. Sport, art and story are not decoration here — they are how hard lessons get practised, rehearsed and remembered.

V.The Proof

Then the corridor becomes a stage.

Certificates — co-signed by partners like MTV Shuga, PATH and Shujaaz — move from table to hand to wall. In February 2026, one school lifted a whole cohort's certificates at once. The photos do not show charity; they show completion.

CodaShe Rises

From silence, she rises — but not alone, and not once. Every term the circle opens again, in Kibera, in Mathare, in Kawangware. The fists come up. The motto above them says what the programme believes.
